serde is part of 4 of my public repositories, from 2016 to 2025.

What it was for: [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (2), [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (1) and [Science and visualisation](@/projects/science.md) (1).

Most recently: [rocksdb\_indexer](@/work/rocksdb-indexer.md); [maze-rs](@/work/maze-rs.md): Maze generation algorithms from the book, in Rust; [sli2dli](@/work/sli2dli.md): SLI to DLI implementation written in rust. Nothing more, nothing less.

1 of these projects runs as a live site.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses serde: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links serde to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
